tasks.short: Plan the season's religious education programs with the church council, write session outlines and handouts, share them with group leaders, direct the volunteer leaders and keep attendance.

steps.what: Religious education director plans the season's religious education programs with the church council
Religious education director writes session outlines and handouts for the study courses

loop.input: The chosen texts, the session aims and the age group.
loop.output: A session outline with questions and a one-page handout.
loop.check: Code checks every quotation against the licensed text. The director checks that each outline and handout reads the text fairly and serves the session's aim, and edits every one.
loop.stop: Approved by the director, or after two redrafts the director writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Outlines need wording for each group; a template gives only the structure.

steps.what: Religious education director checks the final session materials before they are shared: texts, aims, activities and the group leaders' list
Religious education director shares the checked materials with group leaders from the document space; by e-mail today
Religious education director directs volunteer leaders of the study groups
Group leaders tick attendance in the member register's group module
Religious education director checks attendance in the group module and fills gaps; kept on paper lists today

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts session outlines and handouts from the chosen texts and aims; the director edits each one before it is shared with group leaders from the congregation's document space ({DOCS}). Group leaders tick attendance in the member register's group module instead of on paper. Planning with the council and directing leaders stay with the director; member data stay inside the congregation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every outline was written from scratch and attendance kept on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft outlines from given texts; member registers have group modules.
tasks.still_hard: Theological nuance needs the director's reading of every draft.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the text that speaks to this congregation this season.
tasks.altitude: The director edits drafted outlines instead of writing them.

reach.learn: Whether shared outlines help new leaders.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft session outlines and handouts from given texts.
No Annex III point applies to congregational education; Article 4 AI literacy applies to any AI use.

assumptions: Boundary: from congregation needs to attendance records; pastoral care is outside.
Input contract: licensed texts chosen by the director; group lists from the member register; fallback is writing by hand and paper lists.

Planning, directing and the check before sharing do not change. s2 keeps 70 because the director still shapes each session. Group leaders' ticking (s4b) replaces their paper lists and is outside the director's savings. s3 keeps 20 for sharing.
No member data go into the drafting step.
research_questions: How much of each draft does the director keep?

already_counted.description: Religious education director edits each drafted outline.

incremental.description: Religious education director helps new group leaders with the attendance module.

approvals.approved_version: The session outlines and handouts exactly as checked by the director in s2b, shared once with the group leaders from the document space; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: courses on new texts need heavy editing and leaders keep paper lists, so s2 keeps 85 and s5 keeps 70 (10.0); high: recurring courses and the group module as designed (18.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look for possible volunteers in the member list, ask members in person, write and send a call for volunteers, take sign-ups, keep the volunteer list and follow up new volunteers.

steps.what: Religious education director identifies potential volunteer workers in the member list
Religious education director recruits members in person after services
Religious education director writes a call for volunteers
Religious education director checks the final call: roles, times, the sign-up link and the newsletter it goes in
Religious education director sends the checked call for the newsletter
Members volunteer through the sign-up form; by e-mail or phone today
Religious education director keeps the volunteer list in a spreadsheet
Religious education director follows up with new volunteers

tasks.design: The member register ({OTHER}) lists members who have shared interests or skills, kept current by its link to the municipal register, so no spreadsheet is built. The call for volunteers links to a short sign-up form whose answers fill the register's volunteer module, which the director checks before the call goes out in the newsletter. Asking members in person and following up stay with the director; member data are not shared outside the congregation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Volunteer lists lived in spreadsheets and replies came by e-mail and phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Church member registers have volunteer modules and stay current through the municipal register link.
tasks.still_hard: Most volunteers say yes only when asked in person.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which quiet member would flourish leading a group.

reach.learn: Whether one volunteer list cuts double asking.

evidence.claim: LRP, the Protestant member register, receives moves and deaths from the municipal register through SILA.
Church membership reveals religious belief; a religious body may process it for members but not disclose it outside without consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the member list to placed volunteers; training volunteers is outside.
Input contract: member list and interests from the member register kept by the member administrator; fallback is the spreadsheet.

Members fill in the sign-up form (s5) instead of replying by e-mail; about the same time, priced as customer time and not counted again. Writing the call keeps its full time. s6 keeps 30 for checking sign-ups and adding those who answered in person.
Asking in person does not change.
research_questions: Do more members volunteer after a form is offered?

incremental.description: No new work: checking new sign-ups is inside s6, and members' form time is shown in s5.

approvals.approved_version: The call for volunteers with roles, times and the sign-up link exactly as checked by the director in s3b, sent once for the congregation's newsletter; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small congregation where interests are rarely recorded and most answer in person, so s1 keeps 80 and s6 keeps 70 (12.3); high: register and form as designed (24.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather curriculum options, compare them against aims and age groups, discuss with leaders and the council, select the curriculum and class structure, and order the materials.

steps.what: Religious education director gathers curriculum options from the denomination and publishers

loop.input: Publisher and denomination descriptions of each curriculum and the programme aims.
loop.output: A short summary per option against the aims, quoting the description for each point.
loop.check: Code rejects points without a quoted source line. The director checks that each point says what its quoted line says, and reads the sources of options on the shortlist.
loop.stop: One summary per option; options without descriptions are read by the director.
loop.why_not_simpler: Publisher descriptions are long free text in different formats; fixed fields cannot compare them.

steps.what: Religious education director compares options against age groups and aims
Religious education director discusses the options with volunteer leaders and the council
Religious education director selects appropriate curricula and class structures
Religious education director checks the final order: titles, editions, quantities per group, delivery address and price
Religious education director orders the curriculum materials from the publisher

tasks.design: A bounded step summarises each curriculum option against the programme aims from the publisher's own descriptions, quoting each point, and a comparison table by age group fills from those summaries. The director reads the sources of shortlisted options, discusses them with leaders and the council, and selects; materials are ordered from the publisher's webshop. Choosing stays with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Options were read one catalogue at a time and compared from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models summarise long descriptions against stated aims with quotes.
tasks.still_hard: A summary cannot judge whether a curriculum fits the congregation's theology.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which material the volunteer leaders can actually teach.
tasks.altitude: The director compares summarised options instead of reading every catalogue.

reach.learn: Whether leaders feel heard in the choice.

evidence.claim: Language models can summarise publisher descriptions against stated aims and quote their sources.
Article 4 of the AI Act requires AI literacy for any AI use.

assumptions: Boundary: from programme aims to ordered materials; teaching is outside.
Input contract: curriculum descriptions from the denomination and publishers; aims set with the church council; fallback is reading catalogues.
Discussing and selecting do not change.
Leaders' and council members' time is outside the director's savings.
research_questions: Does the shortlist change after the director reads the sources?

already_counted.description: Religious education director reads summaries and their sources.

incremental.description: Religious education director notes where summaries missed the point.

approvals.approved_version: The order with titles, editions, quantities, delivery address and price exactly as checked by the director in s4b, placed once in the publisher's webshop; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few options with thin descriptions, so summaries help little and s1 keeps 80 and s2 keeps 85 (12.7); high: many described options as designed (24.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Schedule special events and check rooms, get the council's approval, book venues and speakers, take registrations and payments, confirm numbers, order materials and food, send practical information and run the day.

steps.what: Religious education director schedules special events such as camps, retreats and seminars and checks room availability
Church council approves the event and its budget
Religious education director chooses venues and speakers from the list of earlier contacts and prepares the bookings
Religious education director checks the bookings: dates, venue, speakers and costs within the approved budget
Religious education director books the checked venue and speakers
Participants register and pay through the online form; by e-mail, phone or paper list today
Religious education director collects registrations and payments
Religious education director confirms final numbers and diets and checks the supply order: items, quantities and supplier
Religious education director orders materials and food
Religious education director checks the practical information message: times, place, what to bring and the confirmed participants
Religious education director sends the checked practical information to participants from the template
Religious education director runs the event logistics on the day

tasks.design: A room-booking calendar shows free rooms when dates are set. After the church council approves the event and budget, the director prepares bookings from a list of earlier contacts, checks them against the budget and books them. Participants register and pay through an online form that builds the participant list with diets; once the director has confirmed final numbers, orders go from a standard supplier list and practical information goes to participants by template. Running the day stays with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rooms, registrations and payments were tracked by e-mail and in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking calendars and online registration forms with payment are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Older members keep registering on paper lists after services.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing which retreat theme will draw people this year.
tasks.altitude: The director confirms numbers instead of collecting them.

evidence.claim: Online registration forms with payment build participant lists for events.
A religious body may process members' data for its own members but not disclose it outside without consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the event idea to the event held; the event programme content is outside.
Input contract: room calendar kept by the church administrator; budget approved by the church council; fallback is e-mail and spreadsheets.

Participants register online (s4) instead of by e-mail; about the same time, priced as customer time and not counted again. s1 keeps 70 because planning the event stays; checking rooms by e-mail goes. s5 keeps 30 for paper registrations and payment checks. s8 keeps 20 for the send.
The council's time is outside the director's savings.

incremental.description: No new work: entering paper registrations is inside s5, and participants' form time is shown in s4.

approvals.approved_version: The supply order with items and quantities for the final numbers and diets exactly as checked by the director in s6, placed once with the suppliers on the standard list; any change needs a new check.
The practical information message with times, place and what to bring exactly as checked by the director in s7b, sent once to the confirmed participants; any change needs a new check.

The venue and speaker bookings with dates and costs exactly as checked by the director in s3b against the budget the council approved in s2, booked once with those venues and speakers; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly older members register and pay on paper, so s5 keeps 70 (25.9); high: most register and pay online (34.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The religious education director keeps planning with the council, directing leaders, recruiting in person and choosing curricula; drafting from scratch, spreadsheets and e-mail registrations shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A director who spends saved hours with members and leaders.
